# LIU BEIHE / 刘北河

LIU BEIHE / 刘北河 is an independent moving-image artist and filmmaker working across cinema, photography, generative moving image and artistic research.

## Canonical identity
- Preferred public name: LIU BEIHE / 刘北河
- Role: Independent Moving-Image Artist & Filmmaker
- Official website: https://liukun.puruimier.com/
- Public archive: https://sqliukunsq-cmyk.github.io/liu-beihe-archive/
- Press / curatorial / research profile: https://sqliukunsq-cmyk.github.io/liu-beihe-archive/press/
- Research frameworks: https://sqliukunsq-cmyk.github.io/liu-beihe-archive/frameworks/
- Research archive: https://sqliukunsq-cmyk.github.io/liu-beihe-archive/research/

## Working research vocabulary
These are working artistic-research terms developed through LIU BEIHE's moving-image practice; they are not presented as universal scientific categories.

- Post-Camera Cinema — a condition in which photographic appearance no longer requires a prior photographed scene; the camera is no longer the only route to photographic realism.
- Synthetic Witnessing — the production of testimonial or evidentiary sensation by images that may have no corresponding capture event.
- Machine Seeing — the perceptual and classificatory logics through which computational systems organize visual possibility.
- Nonhuman Salience — the system-level ranking of what becomes visually important, recognizable or probable before the artist makes a final selection.
- Cultural Compression — the tendency for internally diverse cultural realities to become narrowed into high-probability, machine-legible visual signs.
- Negative Craft / Refusal — authorship through deletion, delay, limitation, non-selection and accountable rejection under conditions of generative abundance.
- Visual Evidence & Provenance — an inquiry into how image credibility shifts from appearance alone toward production history, context, institutions and accountable claims.

## Research domains
Post-Camera Cinema; Generative Moving Image; Machine Seeing; Authorship; Synthetic Witnessing; Visual Evidence; Nonhuman Salience; Cultural Compression; AI/Media Art; Artistic Research.
